text:
Olivia K.: Hi all — first week here. Trying to build the inference runtime from source on a local box with an AMD MI50 (ROCm) and getting linker errors for hip symbols. Anyone seen this before?
Samir P.: welcome! Can you paste the cmake command + the head of the link error?
Olivia K.: cmake .. -DENABLE_HIP=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
Olivia K.: Link error: /usr/bin/ld: libruntime.so: undefined reference to `hipMalloc'
Eli: Which ROCm version are you on? We had ABI breakage between 5.5 and 5.6. Try 5.5 for the fastest repro/compat.
Olivia K.: rocm-smi shows ROCm 5.6.2 on this node
Marie: Also make sure HIP platform env is set: export HIP_PLATFORM=rocm
Marie: And that ROCM_PATH is correct (usually /opt/rocm) and LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /opt/rocm/lib and /opt/rocm/lib64
Olivia K.: I have /opt/rocm/lib in LD_LIBRARY_PATH but hipMalloc still unresolved
Samir P.: Do you have hipcc installed? Run `hipcc --show`. If hipcc is missing some runtime pieces won't link.
Olivia K.: hipcc: command not found
Eli: then the ROCm install is likely incomplete. Which distro? You need the ROCm packages + kernel drivers and headers.
Olivia K.: Ubuntu 22.04, installed from ROCm apt repo, rebooted and ran `sudo modprobe amdgpu`
devops-bot: reminder: check linux-headers-$(uname -r) and GCC version — some ROCm packages require gcc-9 or gcc-10.
Marie: FYI ROCm 5.x tends to prefer gcc-9/10. Newer gcc (11+) can cause ABI/build failures.
Olivia K.: switched to gcc-9 via update-alternatives, re-ran cmake — now hit: relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
Eli: add -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON to your cmake invocation or set CFLAGS='-fPIC' when building third-party libs.
Olivia K.: adding PIC fixed the linker step, thanks! Quick question: for local dev should we be using the container image instead of installing ROCm on host? I'd prefer not to change host packages.
Samir P.: yes, we have a maintained dev image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rocm-dev:2025-05 — it has the recommended ROCm stack and gcc pinned. Use that for consistency. Ping me if you need the registry token.
Olivia K.: tried the container, build succeeded inside the image but perf feels slower than bare-metal; is that expected?
Marie: containers can have different mounts/hugepage configs and cgroup limits. Our dedicated nodes enable hugepages, driver bindings, and CPU governor tweaks — check the container's /etc/rc.local or the dev image README for recommended runtime args (--device /dev/dri, --cap-add SYS_ADMIN sometimes).
Samir P.: I'll paste a short checklist below for onboarding AMD nodes.
Samir P.: checklist: 1) prefer ROCm 5.5 for current runtime; 2) install linux-headers-$(uname -r) and gcc-9/10; 3) export HIP_PLATFORM=rocm and ROCM_PATH=/opt/rocm; 4) ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /opt/rocm/lib64 and /opt/rocm/lib; 5) pass -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON for shared libs; 6) use ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rocm-dev:2025-05 for local dev; 7) modprobe amdgpu and verify hipcc exists; 8) if you see symbol relocation errors, rebuild dependent libs with -fPIC.
Olivia K.: awesome, thanks everyone! :tada:
Samir P.: @Olivia K. if you want a 15m pairing session I can remote in and help set the node up.
Olivia K.: will do, thanks :bow:
